facts.statement: Osmakasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur whose name means "canyon lizard" in the Lakota language.
facts.quote: Osmakasaurus (meaning "canyon lizard", ósmaka meaning "canyon" in the Lakota language) is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur

facts.statement: Osmakasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous Valanginian age in what is now Buffalo Gap, South Dakota, USA.
facts.quote: which lived in the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian age) Chilson Member of the Lakota Formation in what is now Buffalo Gap of South Dakota, United States

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Osmakasaurus was discovered by Nelson Horatio Darton in 1896 in the Lakota Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, USNM 4753, was discovered by Nelson Horatio Darton in 1896 within a layer of the Lakota Formation

facts.statement: The type species O. depressus was originally described in 1909 by Charles W. Gilmore under the name Camptosaurus depressus.
facts.quote: The type species O. depressus was previously referred to as Camptosaurus depressus, and was first described in 1909 by Charles W. Gilmore

facts.statement: In 2008, the species was reclassified into the genus Planicoxa as Planicoxa depressa.
facts.quote: It was assigned to the genus Planicoxa as Planicoxa depressa in 2008

facts.statement: The species was assigned to the new genus Osmakasaurus in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, it was assigned to the new genus Osmakasaurus

facts.statement: Osmakasaurus belongs to the family Camptosauridae within the unranked group Iguanodontia.
Osmakasaurus lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period during the Valanginian, approximately 137 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico durante el Valanginiense, hace aproximadamente 137 millones de años

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Osmakasaurus as extending from the Kimmeridgian to the Barremian (154.8 to 121.4 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Barremian (154.8 to 121.4 million years ago)
